article.title: Can you get income tax notice for UPI, NEFT, RTGS or IMPS transactions? CA explains when your transactions may come under scrutiny - The Economic Times
article.summary: Can you get income tax notice for UPI, NEFT, RTGS or IMPS transactions? CA explains when your transactions may come under scrutiny The Economic Times
article.full_text: Many taxpayers worry that receiving or sending money through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT), Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) and Immediate Payment Service (IMPS) may also invite an income tax notice. With digital payments becoming the norm, such concerns are common, especially when large amounts are involved. However, according to chartered accountant Abhishek Soni, CEO & co-founder of Tax2win, the mode of payment itself is not what attracts the Income Tax Department's attention. Instead, what matters is whether your financial transactions are consistent with the income disclosed in your Income Tax Return (ITR). Soni explains situations when a taxpayer may receive an income tax notice. No, simply using the UPI, NEFT, RTGS, or IMPS does not trigger an income tax notice. These are just payment methods. The Income Tax Department does not issue notices based on how you transfer or receive money. The Income Tax Department looks at whether your transactions match the income you have reported in your Income Tax Return (ITR).For example, you may receive a notice if:You report a low income but your bank account shows large or frequent transactions.You make high-value cash deposits without a valid source. A notice may also be issued if:You make high-value cash deposits without a valid source.Your account receives regular UPI payments that appear to be business income, but you don't report them in your ITR.Source of funds mattersYou may also face scrutiny if you cannot explain the source of money received through the UPI, NEFT, RTGS, or IMPS. Banks report certain high-value transactions, such as large cash deposits, to the Income Tax Department. However, this does not automatically result in a notice. If your transactions are genuine, properly documented, and consistent with the income reported in your ITR, there is generally no cause for concern.

story.title: The QR Code at Closing Time
story.skipLabel: Skip this story about income-tax scrutiny of UPI, NEFT, RTGS and IMPS transactions.

creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: At closing time, a small shop owner must decide whether to accept a rush of digital payments or shut off her QR code, while her anxious brother fears an income-tax notice.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Meera wants to accept the evening’s genuine customer payments and pay her supplier on time.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: Her brother Arjun wants to disable every digital payment method because he fears UPI, NEFT, RTGS or IMPS activity will itself trigger scrutiny.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: A CA explanation makes clear that the payment mode itself does not trigger a notice; consistency with disclosed ITR income and an explainable source of funds matter.
dramaticSpine.reversal: Arjun finds that regular UPI receipts could appear to be business income if Meera does not report them in her ITR.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: Shutting the QR code costs Meera the chance to complete legitimate sales before closing.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: Fear shifts into a practical decision: keep receiving genuine payments while preserving records and reporting income accurately.
dramaticSpine.resolution: Meera leaves the QR code on, saves the transaction records, and prepares to explain the source of funds rather than panic about the payment method.

lines.text: CA Abhishek Soni’s point is clear: the mode itself is not what they look at.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: They look at whether transactions match income disclosed in the ITR.

lines.text: And regular UPI receipts that look like business income? Those need reporting.

beats.turningPoint: The brothers’ abstract fear becomes a concrete choice between a documented genuine payment and money whose source cannot be explained.

visual.caption: Large or frequent transactions and unexplained high-value cash deposits may invite scrutiny.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: Fine. But this cash pile has no source, no story, nothing.

lines.text: Then we do not invent one. We document what we can explain.

visual.caption: Genuine, documented transactions consistent with the ITR are generally not cause for concern.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Keep the QR on. Keep the records. Report the income honestly.

lines.speaker: arjun
lines.text: So the scary part is not UPI—it is money I cannot explain.

lines.speaker: meera
